extracted.intended_audience: Korean central and local government regulators and policy-makers, National Assembly staff, Regulatory Reform Office, SMEs ombudsman, and other stakeholders involved in regulatory policy and reform
extracted.subtask_description: A country peer review of Korea's regulatory policy and reform system, identifying standards, institutional arrangements, tools and recommended practices to improve regulatory quality, stakeholder engagement, impact assessment and enforcement. The document sets criteria for designing, assessing and managing regulation at national and local levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership and oversight of regulatory reform
rubrics_metrics.description: High-level commitment and central oversight (Prime Minister’s Office via the Regulatory Reform Office (RRO)) with a Regulatory Reform Committee (RRC) reviewing regulatory proposals; leadership should steer regulatory policy and coordinate across agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain regulatory reform as a priority; review the role and scope of the RRC to make it more strategic and targeted; secure wider representation (including local administration) within the RRC; enhance the secretariat function to dedicate resources to high-impact proposals; use ministerial meetings to focus on reducing burdens and creating a business-friendly environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target regulations by expected impact (use RRC selectively)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory review resources should focus on the most burdensome and high-impact regulations rather than checking all impact assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the RRC to review only the most burdensome regulations; introduce incentives for central administrative agencies to conduct 'self-oversight' on low-burden regulations; enable fast-tracking for less-burdensome regulations and grant 'regulatory autonomy' to agencies that demonstrate good processes and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact analysis (RIA) requirements and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory Impact Analysis Statements (RIAS) are prepared by agencies and reviewed; RIAS should compare regulatory costs and benefits and include plans for ex post evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft RIAS through an online e-RIA platform that automatically compares regulatory costs and benefits; require RIAS for proposals (with standard and simplified RIA types as appropriate); improve the quality of RIAs and ensure the evidence base is strengthened (including independent research inputs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-in, Cost-out (CICO) constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: A system that restricts the cost increase of new or amended regulations by abolishing or relaxing regulations that produce equal or greater costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply CICO to manage the flow of regulation by offsetting regulatory costs of new proposals with elimination of existing burdens; integrate CICO analysis into RIA/RIAS and submit to oversight bodies and legislature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex post evaluation and planned evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce and publish ex post evaluations for existing regulations and discuss planned evaluations to assess whether regulations meet intended objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an ex post evaluation plan as part of each RIAS; introduce ex post evaluation strategically (targeting high-impact or uncertain regulations); publicly discuss and publish planned evaluations to improve transparency and learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of quality control into regulatory reduction initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality control systems should be embedded into initiatives that reduce or remove regulations to ensure removed/altered rules still meet intended objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear and systematic criteria when reducing regulations; guarantee that regulations meet intended objectives as perceived by regulated entities and implementers; develop and use metrics that show the added value of regulatory quality initiatives adopted by executive and legislature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement and transparency in rule-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Central administrative agencies must engage relevant stakeholders (including local administration) early and transparently in the rule-making process; make regulatory proposals and analysis publicly available (e.g., portals like i-Ombudsman, Sinmungo, Regulatory Information Portal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengthen stakeholder engagement capacity within public administration; define clear accountability rules to manage expectations on engagement; ensure stakeholder engagement (including local administration) in National Assembly law-making, especially for member-initiated bills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusiveness of regulatory institutions and processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Open institutions and processes to a wider range of stakeholders (private sector, local government, public, National Assembly) to make the system more transparent and inclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broaden RRC composition beyond private-sector orientation to include other stakeholders; encourage private sector to shift from complaint-focused to solution-finding; create channels for local governments to be involved early in drafting to ensure relevance and implementability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative regulatory quality checks (National Assembly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish legislative mechanisms that check regulatory quality within the National Assembly so that laws originating there receive the same rigour as the executive's regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a permanent legislative regulatory quality check mechanism; require the executive to submit RIA statements and CICO analyses to the National Assembly to inform bill drafting and review; build socio-economic analysis capacity inside the legislature (or use automatic review/post-implementation evaluation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretariat capacity and resourcing for oversight bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Oversight bodies (e.g., RRO/RRC) need sufficient, skilled staff to review the large volume of regulatory proposals and to improve quality rather than merely checking compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhance secretariat function and staffing to guarantee resources are dedicated to high-impact proposals; ensure adequate analytical capability to perform robust reviews and follow-up; address the imbalance where ~3 500 proposals are submitted but only ~20 staff review them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory registry and information portals
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a central, publicly accessible registry/portal for regulatory proposals, registered regulations, RIAS and regulatory reform progress to improve transparency and ease stakeholder engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish regulatory proposals and RIA statements online; provide user-customised search and one-click services (e.g., for SMEs) and maps that show high-frequency complaint regulations for regional comparison; ensure online systems accept feedback in multiple languages as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic regulatory policy and prioritisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a clear strategy and vision for regulatory policy to make smarter use of resources and target reforms where they yield the highest economic and social impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the regulatory system more strategic, targeted, proactive and inclusive; prioritise reforms that simplify and improve regulations most burdensome for business and citizens; use forward-looking bodies (e.g., Investment Committee on Emerging Industry) for new industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive regulatory management (shift from complaint-driven)
rubrics_metrics.description: Move from a largely complaint-driven system to proactive identification and implementation of regulatory improvements by central agencies and shared ownership with the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign responsibilities to central administrative agencies for proactively identifying improvements; create incentives and channels for private sector to participate in solution-finding; encourage agencies to develop and report on self-oversight practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-based approach to enforcement, inspection and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt risk-based enforcement and inspection strategies at central and local levels to allocate scarce inspection and enforcement resources effectively, especially in areas like occupational safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop shared information systems that collect data on probability and impact of risks and use compliance/inspection data for targeting; ensure enforcement decisions are evidence-based and subject to scrutiny; increase staff and capability in enforcement agencies where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination between central and local governments
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure vertical and horizontal coordination so local governments can implement, interpret and enforce regulations consistently and feed experience back to central policy-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly discuss and coordinate across local governments (regional-regional and regional-sub-regional); create channels to bring local experience upstream to central agencies; support common standards for enforcement and inspection at local level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory quality management inside agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should have internal procedures and capacity to manage regulatory quality, including simplified RIA procedures for low-burden measures and the ability to earn regulatory autonomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require agencies to set up internal quality control, reporting and training; allow fast-tracking for low-burden regulations while holding agencies accountable through reporting and outcomes; integrate quality control into regulatory reduction initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity-building and training for regulators
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide training, syllabi and capacity-building programmes for regulatory management across central and local administrations to improve RIA, stakeholder engagement and enforcement skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement online/offline training (sample syllabi exist) and continuous professional development; strengthen analytical skills for socio-economic analysis and RIA preparation; build capacity for legislative staff in the National Assembly where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance assessment and monitoring of regulatory initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Use indicators, surveys and metrics (e.g., iREG, customer satisfaction surveys, monitoring of regulatory reduction achievements) to assess regulatory performance and the impact of reforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor progress of regulatory reduction initiatives; use assessments (e.g., survey items for compliance measurement) and publish results; develop metrics that show added value and impact on businesses, citizens and enforcement bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: SME-focused regulatory relief and tailoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and deliver regulatory practices that reduce burdens on SMEs, recognising their limited capacity relative to large firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce compliance costs for SMEs by making regulations more flexible; provide extra time or grace periods for SMEs to comply with new regulations; ensure SMEs understand rights and have accessible appeal processes; during annual RRC reporting provide assessment of impacts on SMEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored RIA and reform process for SMEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use SME-specific regulatory impact analysis and reform procedures (including consultation, ombudsman, sunset clauses and user-based web systems) to identify vulnerable businesses and prioritise reforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply small business RIA processes and review steps (finding unreasonable regulations → in-depth analysis for alternatives → concentrated consultation → regulatory improvement); conduct SME regulatory cost surveys and in-depth interviews to estimate direct and administrative costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and user-access for SME regulatory reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Make SME regulatory reform processes transparent and accessible (one-click services, compass/regulatory map, online complaint channels), allowing businesses to track reforms and submit comments (including anonymously).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorise reform cases by user types and industry; present implementation status, allow navigation by industry/region/company characteristics; publish complaint frequencies and map results regionally to prioritise action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunset clauses and periodic validity review
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sunset clauses and periodic review to verify the continued validity of regulations and task agencies to revise regressive rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply sunset clauses to review regulations; require agencies to consider SME burden when revising existing regulations; report on outcomes and follow-up implementation (implemented/delayed/withheld).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource adequacy and workload management for oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure oversight bodies are properly resourced and their workload is managed so they can provide substantive review rather than superficial checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address disproportionate workloads (e.g., thousands of proposals vs small secretariat); limit detailed RRC review to proposals of consequence; provide incentives and mechanisms for agencies to self-certify low-burden items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of independent and external analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplement government RIAs with independent research institutions or external analysis to strengthen evidence and impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage research institutions with autonomy to provide analysis on specific issues; ensure independent inputs inform RIA and RRC deliberations to improve credibility and quality of assessments.
